description:
FILED s486a (2026-09-16) by tools/cause-census.pl, which is why it was visible
at all: the XDIFF population is not-supported BY CONSTRUCTION (every registered
file cites a docs/not-supported.md section in baselines/perl-suite-expected.tsv,
and baselines/perl-suite-expected-rows.tsv holds that file's blessed diverging
rows), so a row there classing as `unexplained` means the two files disagree
about which files are registered.

MEASURED: perl-suite-expected.tsv has 112 file rows; perl-suite-expected-rows.tsv
has 2,517 rows over 113 DISTINCT files.  The extra file is

    mro/inconsistent_c3_utf8.t   (1 blessed row)

Its ASCII sibling IS registered:

    mro/inconsistent_c3.t   not-supported.md \x{a7}mro + \x{a7}error-text -- C3 merge-failure error wording differs

so the reason row is simply missing -- almost certainly the utf8 twin was not
added when the sibling was, the same way the other mro/*_utf8.t twins were.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE ROW: baselines/perl-suite-expected.tsv's own header
says the reasons there EXCUSE the rows blessed in the -rows.tsv file.  A row
whose file has no reason is excused by nothing; and the enforcement runs the
other way (an extra ROW keeps a registered file DIFF), so this shape -- a row
for an UNREGISTERED file -- is not checked by anything today.

FIRST STEPS: (1) run tools/run-perl-suite.pl on t/mro/inconsistent_c3_utf8.t and
read what it diverges on; (2) if it is the same error-wording divergence as the
sibling, add the reason row with the same citation and re-bless the rows; (3)
consider making the runner (or tools/t/audit-instruments.t) fail when
perl-suite-expected-rows.tsv names a file perl-suite-expected.tsv does not --
the missing half of the existing STALE/intruder checks.
subject: mro/inconsistent_c3_utf8.t has a blessed XDIFF ROW but no REASON row -- the one row in that population the class rule cannot class
